title.purpose: Client names, modal titles, the sidebar brand mark.

label.purpose: Uppercase mono labels: eyebrows, table headers, form labels.

data.purpose: Every table cell, badge, and numeric input; tabular numerals.

motion.name: sidebar-collapse
motion.purpose: Sidebar width transition when collapsing/expanding the nav.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: Below this width the sidebar drops above the content and loses its sticky/scroll behavior.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The system's one filled, high-emphasis action.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 12px; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; background: #0a493c; color: #ffffff; border: none; padding: 7px 13px; transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #48a278; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #e2f5ef; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { background: #d2d2d2; color: #67706d; cursor: default; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 11.5px; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; background: transparent; border: 1px solid #d2d2d2; color: #67706d; padding: 7px 12px; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { border-color: #23272b; color: #23272b; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #e2f5ef; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard field: search boxes, numeric entry, settings.
components.css: .ds-input { height: 34px; border: 1px solid #d2d2d2; border-radius: 4px; padding: 0 9px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 12.5px; background: #ffffff; color: #23272b; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #b5b5b5; } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: #48a278; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #e2f5ef; }

components.name: Status Pill — Good
components.css: .ds-pill { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 10px; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 99px; border: 1px solid #d2d2d2; color: #67706d; white-space: nowrap; display: inline-block; } .ds-pill-good { color: #0a493c; border-color: #48a278; background: #e2f5ef; }

components.name: Status Pill — Bad
components.css: .ds-pill-bad { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 10px; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 99px; color: #d1453b; border: 1px solid #d1453b; background: #fbe7e4; display: inline-block; white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Nav Item (current)
components.description: The sidebar's "you are here" state — Mint tint fill with a Logo Teal wayfinding border.
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; padding: 7px 18px; color: #23272b; text-decoration: none; font-family: Montserrat, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: #e2f5ef; color: #0a493c; } .ds-nav-item-current { background: #e2f5ef; color: #0a493c; font-weight: 600; border-right: 3px solid #3bc9ac; }

components.name: Summary Cell
components.description: A single KPI tile inside the dashboard's summary strip.
components.css: .ds-summary-cell { background: #ffffff; padding: 12px 14px; border: 1px solid #d2d2d2; } .ds-summary-label { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 9px; color: #67706d; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-summary-value { font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 18px; font-weight: 700; margin-top: 4px; color: #0a493c; }

narrative.overview:
This is an operator's console for running the numbers, not a marketing surface — every screen exists so Boris (and, as their pages come online, EMG's finance/ops staff and account managers) can see exactly where the agency's money and staffing hours stand. The voice is precise and institutional: controlled, exact, unshowy. Density and hairline borders read as rigor, not clutter — a page with forty rows of tabular figures is the system working as intended, not a page that needs simplifying.

Two fonts carry the whole identity. Montserrat speaks — every heading, every sentence of prose. IBM Plex Mono counts — every label, every table cell, every number, every badge. The moment you're reading a figure, the typeface itself tells you you're in the ledger, not the prose. Two colors carry the emphasis: Deep Ledger Green is the system's authority (headers, totals, positive figures), and Signal Gold is reserved entirely for the one line that matters most on the forecast chart — net profit. Everything else is neutral: paper, hairlines, slate.

The system is flat by rule. There is no drop shadow anywhere in this design language — elevation is expressed only through hairline borders and background contrast. (Two implementation spots — the deal-editor modal and the line-item cards — currently still carry a soft shadow; that's drift from this rule, not sanctioned exceptions, and should be brought to flat the next time either is touched.)
keyCharacteristics: A locked, closed brand palette — two greens, one gold, one teal, functional red/amber. No new accent colors.
Montserrat for words, IBM Plex Mono for numbers — never swapped, never mixed within one element.
Flat surfaces, hairline dividers, zero shadows by rule.
Dense, tabular, laptop-disciplined: charts scale to their container, table names truncate before they wrap, horizontal scroll is a last resort.
Settled data reads at full strength; forecast/projected data reads visually lighter — the system always shows you which numbers are real.

rules.name: The One Gold Rule
rules.body: Signal Gold appears in exactly one place: the forecast chart's net line. It is not a general accent, a warning color, or a highlight — its rarity is what makes it legible as "the number that matters."

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Montserrat speaks; IBM Plex Mono counts. A heading, a sentence, a button label — Montserrat. A number, a table cell, a badge, a column header — IBM Plex Mono. Never swap them, never mix them within one element.

rules.name: The Micro-Scale Rule
rules.body: New chrome text uses a step from the Chrome scale (9px-22px, fixed); new deal-editor controls use a step from the Editor micro-scale (0.56rem-0.82rem, fluid). Don't invent a new literal size — pick the closest existing step, or extend the scale deliberately if none fits.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Rule Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow anywhere. Depth is hairline borders and background contrast only.

rules.name: The Brand Rule Line
rules.body: A boundary that matters gets a 2px Deep-Ledger-Green underline; every lesser division gets a 1px hairline in --line. The weight of the border tells you how important the seam is.

dos: Do keep Signal Gold to exactly one job: the forecast chart's net line.
Do write every heading and sentence in Montserrat, and every number, label, badge, and column header in IBM Plex Mono — never swap them.
Do mark a real section boundary with a 2px Deep-Ledger-Green rule line, and everything smaller with a 1px hairline.
Do keep Alert Rust and Alert Amber reserved for their alert meanings only — never decorative.
Do let charts scale to their container and let table names truncate rather than wrap or force horizontal scroll (The Laptop Discipline Rule).
Do render settled data at full color strength and projected/forecast data visually lighter, everywhere the distinction applies — not just in the flagship chart.
donts: Don't add box-shadow anywhere; this system is flat by rule. Bring the modal and line-card's current shadows to border-based separation next time either is touched.
Don't introduce a new accent color outside this closed palette (two greens, one gold, one teal, functional red/amber).
Don't use Logo Teal for anything beyond the current-nav-item indicator and the sidebar toggle icon — it is a wayfinding mark, not a decorative accent.
Don't use Signal Gold anywhere but the forecast chart's net line — not a pill border, not a warning state, not a highlight.
